tasks.title: Make point-of-use rating reachable
tasks.note: **`/end` is the wrong and only moment** (Aaron's question, Session 49). Ratings happen once, at `/end`, in a batch where the agent retro-rates a dozen entries long after the reasoning they informed. **Rating at *retrieval* is not the fix** — at recall time you know the match was plausible, not that it helped, so it measures the retriever rather than the knowledge, and retrieval is *already* recorded deterministically (`recall_count`, `last_recalled_at`, `recall_log`: 685 recalls across 175 of 357 entries). The right moment is point-of-use: when an entry demonstrably changes a decision, minutes after recall. **`ob_feedback` is already callable at any time — nothing enforces `/end`.** The actual blocker is that `/start` injects recalled entries as prose without their IDs, so mid-session rating is not *reachable*. Surfacing `[id]` alongside each injected entry is the small deterministic unblock; keep `/end` as the sweep for whatever went unrated in flight. Pairs with the apoptosis item above — earlier timing alone will not produce a "harmful" the rater was never going to give. Current coverage: **104 entries recalled but never rated**, 80 of 357 ever rated.

tasks.title: v0.15.1 made a foreign `.recalled-entries.json` writer unreachable *and* uncountable
tasks.note: (Session 50, surfaced by Prime). Prime confirmed it does not write that path, then correctly advised refusing foreign writers loudly anyway — a future harness version is not bound by today's inventory. That property cannot be built as described: v0.15.1's fix was not a `session_id` comparison but the **removal of the read** (precedence: explicit ids → `recall_log` → the file only if the session is unknown → nothing). On the normal path there is no read, so no refusal, so nothing to report. Net effect: **"no foreign writer" and "a foreign writer never looked at" are the same observation from inside the resolver.** This is a fourth instance of the dropped-count invariant above, sitting inside the fix that shipped this morning — the bad case was made unreachable and thereby uncountable. Fix: split observation from authority — a detector that reads the file purely to *report* and never to resolve ids, preserving the structural guarantee that the file cannot influence which entries get rated. Do **not** reopen v0.15.1; the correctness fix is right, this adds detection on top. General form worth carrying: **removing a read is not the same as counting what you no longer read** — structural prevention makes a failure impossible and simultaneously invisible, which is correct while the failure cannot recur and a blind spot the moment a new writer can appear.

tasks.title: Add a `/sync` validator for the `.agents/skills/` frontmatter contract, asserting all three identity sources agree
tasks.note: (Session 50, reported by Prime). Prime's harness loads `<repo>/.agents/skills/*/SKILL.md` at boot and found three malformed: `gotchas/` and `seo-optimizer-test/` have a frontmatter `name` that differs from the directory, and `self-improving-agent-guide/SKILL.md` **had no frontmatter at all** so it never loaded — a 192-line architecture document invisible to the router for months (frontmatter added this session; unverified until Prime reboots). Neither reader was wrong about its own file; nothing ever checked they described the same set. Validator belongs in `/sync`, **not** the session-end hook — `/sync` is the mandatory pre-commit gate, the hook runs unattended after the fact. Confirmed hand-written, not generated: nothing in the repo writes that path, so there is no emitter to fix instead. **Directory work DONE 2026-08-11** — Aaron greenlit both. `gotchas/` renamed to `self-improving-agent-gotchas/` with INDEX.md's Directory cell updated; all three identity sources now verified in agreement for both remaining skills. `seo-optimizer-test/` moved out of the loader path to `.agents/archive/seo-optimizer-generalized.md` — **archived, not deleted, because the "leftover fixture" call was wrong.** It is the *generalized derivative* of TCM's applied `seo-optimizer` (placeholders instead of the hardcoded domain, `[COMMON]`/`[ARCHITECTURAL]`/`[SUBTLE]` tier annotations, plus a Priority Framework and two checklists existing in no other copy — 87 unique content lines). The `-test` suffix was recording a skill-generalization test *output*. Aaron to decide its permanent home. **Lesson worth keeping:** Forge and Prime independently agreed it was a fixture and the agreement read as corroboration — but both had reasoned from the same three indirect signals (`-test` suffix, absence from INDEX.md, wrong subject for the repo) and **neither had opened the file**. Two readers, one evidence set: the convergence carried no more information than either conclusion alone. Remaining scope of this item is the `/sync` validator itself. Original blocked items were: rename `gotchas/` → `self-improving-agent-gotchas/`, and decide `seo-optimizer-test/` — a Next.js SEO skill in a memory-protocol repo, unregistered in INDEX.md, which both agents read as a leftover test fixture (and which is currently the only skill Prime auto-triggers that no human ever declared). **The rename is cheaper than first assessed** (Prime, verified): INDEX.md's *Skill* column already reads `self-improving-agent-gotchas` and only its *Directory* cell says `gotchas/`, so the rename edits one table cell and lands all three identity sources in agreement — no name reconciliation across the registry. Whoever wrote INDEX.md had already judged `gotchas` too generic.

tasks.title: Commit the entry-455 archive move as one commit
tasks.note: (Session 53, deferred by Aaron — two minutes). The vault has ` D Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/wikiskill-paper-vs-sia-memory-layer.md` alongside an untracked `Archive/` holding a byte-identical copy (2287 bytes). Stage **both together** — `git add "Archive/" "Experiences/Self-Improving-Agent/wikiskill-paper-vs-sia-memory-layer.md"` — so git records a **rename** and `--follow` traces through it; committing the deletion alone would leave the archive as an untracked file git cannot protect. tasks.title: Retire the mailbox as *transport*, keep it as *archive
tasks.note: * (Aaron's ask, Session 53; spec at `docs/mailbox-transport-retirement-spec.md`). **The protocol is SIA's, the store is not** — reader `pipelines/session-start/agent-identity.ts` (`readMailboxState`), emitter `cli-bootstrap.ts:135–141`, and it **ships to every template consumer** via `project-template/.agents/AGENT.md:5,14–21` and `start.md:54`; the data lives in `~/.agents/`, a separate repo, and `/sync` validates none of it. Note the name collision — `<project>/.agents/` (gitignored, `.gitignore:9`) is not `~/.agents/`. **The archive half works** (26 commits, 25 touching message files, truncate-to-latest ran clean at `6454bbc`); the transport half is obsolete. Session 53 is its own evidence: Aaron hand-carried the inbox file, Forge then reached Atlas live four times, and the live channel **corrected the file twice** (v0.17.0 had already shipped; delta numbering moved from `#5 before #2` to names after 455/456 renumbered) — so the reply committed at `44dfd8b` was stale on both counts *within the session that wrote it*. **Root cause is one function.** In `readMailboxState`, `lastDecision` parses `^## (\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})` and sorts — date-aware; `messageCount` counts `^## \[` with no age, ever. The durable half already knows about time and the ephemeral half does not, which is why five dead channels (TCM 2026-04-24, worthit 06-04, nexcrm 06-09, a2a-hub and openlaser 07-22) announce themselves identically to the one live one. **Same dropped-count invariant as the four instances in P1** — a letter has no status field, cannot represent *answered* or *superseded*, so absence of resolution reads as currency. **Fix (deterministic-first rule #2, remove the trigger):** surface a message **only when it postdates its channel's last decision** — no timeout constant, nothing to tune, cannot drift; unparseable headers count as unresolved and are *reported*, not skipped. Then document live `SendMessage` as primary with the mailbox as the fallback for a peer that isn't running, state the durable contract (*if it must survive the session it is a decision or a task, written in that form*), and move the five dead channels under `archive/`. **Stageable today with no code change** — a blank `mailbox_channel` already skips the surface (`AGENT.md:21`); the code change only sets the default. Supersedes the item below, which asked for the same thing from the other end. Do **not** conflate the `AGENT.md` edits with the personalization-leak item in P0 — same file, separate changes. (Session 53)

tasks.title: An unrecognised CLI flag must refuse, not select the mutating default
tasks.note: Session 62: `node open-brain/build/cli.js sync --check-only` was run intending a dry run. There is no such flag. cli.ts:21 is `args.includes("--check")` — exact array membership, so "--check-only" does not match, checkOnly stayed false, the flag was SILENTLY DISCARDED and sync ran in FIX MODE, writing seven tracked files plus untracked PRD.md. No harm that time only because every write was version-sync the release bump required anyway, and the diff was read before committing — WHICH MEANS THE SAFETY CAME FROM THE OPERATOR, NOT THE TOOL. Loop 11's other 38 defects were prose that lied about behaviour; this is behaviour that lies about intent, and it is the more dangerous class: a mistyped safety flag selects the unsafe path and says nothing. Fix: parse argv against a known flag set and exit non-zero on anything unrecognised, naming the flag. Deterministic, and it cannot be overridden the way a documented convention can. Applies to every subcommand of cli.ts, not just sync. Evidence: cli.ts:21, and the seven-file write at 811dddc's parent. --- SIGHTING, session 80 (Forge, developer), relayed by the planner at session 78 and labelled as the developer's observation: `node open-brain/build/cli.js sync --help` at 5759008 did NOT print help; it ran the full sync in FIX mode, the mutating default. `git status` afterwards showed nothing changed, which was luck rather than a refusal. This is the exact failure this task names, observed live on the command every seat runs before every commit. Reproduce: that command at 5759008. SECOND EXPOSURE, same session, planner's own: a Bash one-liner quoting this sighting in double quotes let the shell execute the backticked command itself before node parsed anything. The tree was clean afterwards. A command that mutates by default is one quoting slip away from running unasked. — Closed session 148: DONE per record 199b audit (711d700). 686eef5 on master; cli-flags.test.ts. Forge probed a fresh bf33fe4 build in a temp dir: sync --bogus, sync -dry-run, sync --check-only, detach -dry-run, state migrate -dry-run and start --bogus each exited 2 and named the token. Record 199 (the planner's brief for this task) was moot: the brief was written from the open list without checking source.

tasks.title: The test suite is not type-checked at all
tasks.note: open-brain/tsconfig.json is `"include": ["src/**/*"]` and there is exactly one tsconfig, so `tsc` NEVER READS open-brain/tests/. Not 'checked less strictly' — not checked. Found in Loop 12 R-010: cutting `enableHeuristicRatings` left the flag named in six places across four test files and `npx tsc --noEmit` exited 0. The referrers surfaced only at runtime, when assertions happened to trip on them. This reframes '603 tests passing': the suite proves behaviour, and nothing proves the tests' own types. A type error in a test is invisible unless a runtime assertion happens to catch it. Fix is a tsconfig that includes tests (or a second one for typecheck only); the risk is that it surfaces a backlog of existing test type errors, which is the point. Independent of the retirement work — filed, not fixed, in the loop that found it.

tasks.title: Shadow merge gate: the runtime records what it would have done at each merge, and disagreements with Aaron are counted
tasks.note: DERIVED FROM THE AUTONOMY RULING (see the decision recorded this revision). At every point where a merge to master could occur, the runtime writes a would-merge / would-not-merge verdict with its reasons — deterministic check results, QA E_t status, and once the gates exist, their typed answers — into artifacts/iterations/tNNN/. tasks.title: 'Run the full suite alone' must become a check: assert peer idleness before the run and refuse or flag when a peer is busy
tasks.note: Opened session 77 on Aaron's ruling. THE RULE NAMES A CONDITION NO SEAT COULD VERIFY. 'Run the full suite alone at every candidate' has been in briefs since Loop 16 and every seat believed it was following it; the QA seat's slice-three baseline was run 'alone' while the planner was demonstrably active mid-run (a rulings message arrived during it) and the developer was working G-045, and it went red. A seat that believes it ran alone has an instrument that cannot tell 'nothing else was running' from 'I did not look' - G-044's class, in the one rule meant to guard the measurement. PROJECT DOCTRINE SETTLES THE FIX: a rule someone has to remember is an intention; a check is a rule. THE CHECK IS NOW POSSIBLE AND WAS DONE BY HAND TONIGHT: ListAgents lists every peer session on the machine with a busy/idle state, and calling it immediately before the suite is what made V-076's measurement mean anything. Without it the clean idle run would have been one more unlabelled data point in a table of eleven. SHAPE: before a full-suite run at a candidate, the seat calls ListAgents; if any peer is busy it REFUSES or flags loudly in the report, and either way the peer states at run time are recorded ALONGSIDE the result so a later reader can tell a contended run from a clean one. Every historical sighting lacks that field, which is why eleven measurements cannot be re-read. LIMITS TO BUILD IN, from this session's own findings: ListAgents has a REGISTRATION LAG - the developer's listing showed only the planner while the QA seat was already running - so an early or short listing is indistinguishable from a machine with nothing on it, and the check must not read an empty listing as 'idle' without a control (D-029 records this). It also cannot see non-Claude load (a build, a browser, an indexer), so it is a necessary and not a sufficient condition and must be worded as such rather than as a guarantee of idleness. RELATED: G-042 (the fault this protects the measurement of), V-076 (the controlled comparison), T-166 (another instrument that reported confidence it had not earned). --- AMENDED session 78, and Aaron ruled the policy (D-034): THE PEER SET IS NO LONGER ONLY SIA'S SEATS. On 2026-09-23 around 02:14Z the A2A-Hub planner seat (worktrees-82, a different project on the same machine) was BUSY during the developer's full suite on candidate A's working tree. Run 1 exited 1 with G-042's signature (1096 passed, 2 skipped, 1 unhandled onTaskUpdate timeout). Run 2 was clean after that seat was asked to make no tool calls. The developer and QA seats agree that both surviving hypotheses are LOAD, either external (the other project's seat) or the suite's own (candidate A adds about 153s of spawning at full parallelism), and that neither is separated yet. An interactive seat can also show BUSY while its human types. POLICY (D-034): other projects' seats work normally BY DEFAULT and are RECORDED beside every SIA suite result; they pause only when a SIA seat requests a controlled rerun. THE DETERMINISTIC NEXT STEP, replacing a request someone must remember with a condition code can check: a machine-wide 'suite running' marker (a lock file in a shared location, for example under ~/.claude/, carrying the owning session and start time) that the suite writes at start and removes at end, and that any session's heavy command checks first, recording rather than refusing by default under D-034. It must be stale-safe: a marker from a crashed run expires by age or by its owner's absence from ListAgents.

tasks.title: Memory is LOOKUP by default and INJECTION only on a deterministic match against the act; fix the WRITE side first, so every stored lesson carries the key (command pattern, path or error string) that would have caught the mistake
tasks.note: Session 78, planner's recommendation, recorded at Aaron's request ('capture your recommendation about the fix'). NOT A RULING; Aaron has not decided it. THE SPLIT, by one question: does the agent know it needs something? (a) YES: LOOKUP. ob_recall is called with trigger 'explicit' when the agent asks. Evidence: Loop 10 measured session-start injection at p=0.688 once topic-matched, while ranking earned its keep at p=0.035; CLAUDE.md, delivered at 100% reliability, failed to change behaviour (the upper bound); HoH gained with no memory module, using an index plus fetch-on-demand. (b) NO: LOOKUP CANNOT HELP, and this is the case the PRD's 'lessons from past mistakes are forgotten' names. G-039: the store held entry 299 and the agent made that mistake anyway, because it never knew to ask. Injection is the only mechanism for this case. HOW INJECTION KNOWS WHAT IS RELEVANT: only by deriving it from the ACT, never from the session's topic, which is what failed at session start. Three act signatures, all concrete and all present at the moment it matters: (1) command shape, which is what the Loop 16 trigger does; (2) the file being edited; (3) ERROR TEXT, probably the highest-value one, since an error is exactly when an agent is about to take a known-wrong path, and error strings match precisely. Precision only, silent below the floor, as the trigger already works. THE BOTTLENECK IS THE WRITE SIDE, NOT RETRIEVAL: injection can only match an entry that carries a machine-matchable key. G-017 measured 86% of ACTION lines as prose that names no file or command, so those entries can never be injected precisely whatever the matcher does. QA's entry 615 is the same finding from the other side: two costly Loop 16 errors were in the store and unreachable. THE FIX, IN ORDER: (i) at store time (/end A12, ob_store), a lesson must carry the key that would have caught it: a command pattern, a path glob or an error signature. An entry without one is lookup-only by construction, and that is reported, not hidden; (ii) extend the trigger past Bash command shape to file-edit and tool-error events, keyed on those fields rather than on a hand-maintained element table (T-162); (iii) keep session-start injection OFF (Loop 10 C2). STILL UNPROVEN, stated so nobody builds on it as settled: four injections, all entry 299, all apt, none changed behaviour, because the practice was already loaded every time. The discriminating observation is an injection on a mistake the agent has NOT already internalised; the trigger_fires table is the instrument. Relates to G-017, G-026, G-039, T-159, T-162.

tasks.title: The main tree serves every session and nothing says when it is behind master: the greeting must print the SERVING build's distance from origin/master, and one refusing command must update, rebuild and verify it
tasks.note: Session 78, raised by Aaron's question ('so we need to rebuild after every loop and make sure the mcp server is on latest?'). The answer today is yes, by hand: after any merge touching open-brain/src, update the main checkout to master, rebuild, and have every open session run /mcp reconnect open-brain. That is a step that works only while someone remembers it, and it was missed. MEASURED 2026-09-22: the main tree was at 0bf0597, 24 commits behind origin/master 9788064, while every check read green, because build-freshness compares the main tree's build to the main tree's own HEAD and never to master (G-034). The SessionStart hook prints a tree-currency line for the seat's own checkout but none for the checkout actually serving the hooks and the MCP server. FIX SHAPE, deterministic first: (1) cli-bootstrap prints, first, 'serving build: <sha>, N behind origin/master (last fetch <time>)' for the MAIN tree, however the session was launched; it reads refs locally and never fetches; (2) one command, e.g. `open-brain main-tree update`, which refuses on a dirty tree or on commits not on origin/master (the detach command's three refusals), fast-forwards, rebuilds, and reads build-freshness back against origin/master rather than trusting exit codes. It then says which sessions must reconnect, because only the human can. The reconnect cannot be automated from inside a session. Relates to G-033, G-034, T-154. — FINDING, planner session 150 (from T-201's stop): StateSchema is z.strictObject at every level, so ANY new field written to master's record blinds every checkout whose build predates it, including the main tree that serves every session's MCP server. T-158 (merged d5dfa74) already added optional GapSchema fields (status, closed_session, closed_rev). The first close_gap tombstone that reaches master will therefore make every not-yet-rebuilt build fail to parse the record. It is dormant until then, and it is a real reason for this task: the serving build must be rebuilt when a schema-changing merge lands, and a refusing command must say so. Until it ships: rebuild the main tree (npm install, not npm ci) before the first close_gap after d5dfa74, and tell the QA PC's main checkout the same.

tasks.title: Per-stage effort chosen by a deterministic policy, with Jev in shadow. Sequenced AFTER candidate A (it needs ProcessRole)

DESIGN SHAPE, the developer's to design and the planner's to rule: (1) DETERMINISTIC FIRST, a policy file (data, zod-validated, JSON Schema derived and drift-checked, like the gate policies) mapping what the runtime already knows to an effort level: the stage (QA -> max); the plan's paths (security-relevant harness files such as refwatch/git/runtime -> xhigh; docs and version surfaces -> medium); a retry after a failed attempt -> one level up. (2) JEV ONLY FOR WHAT PATHS CANNOT SEE, as a typed judgement ('does this plan need novel reasoning or is it mechanical?'): a one-line diff to a git primitive is small and subtle, which is the shape of this session's two false claims ('no compare-and-swap possible', 'the overrides close config'). (3) JEV RUNS IN SHADOW FIRST: it records the level it WOULD have chosen beside the policy's, and changes nothing until its disagreements are counted against outcomes, T-155's discipline applied to effort. HOH-JEV section 3: typed output guarantees the interface, not the truth. THE OUTCOME DATA ALREADY STARTED: from dispatch-2 (PRs #104/#105) every tracked report records model AND effort, and the instrument is the session transcript's PER-ENTRY `effort` field, reported as timestamped runs. settings.json gives only the configured default, as the QA seat found with three instruments giving three answers. tasks.title: Win32 job-object launcher so the role's whole process tree is killed on a NORMAL exit too (R22's named limit on Windows)
tasks.note: Session 78, from rulings-4 (R22 narrowed to option (b) on the developer's costing). Node has no job-object API. taskkill /T walks from a LIVE root, so after a role exits normally its orphans are unreachable, and descendant PID lists (WMI/CIM) are racy against PID reuse and were ruled out. Candidate A therefore kills the process group on POSIX on every exit path, and on win32 states in every iteration record that normal-exit tree-kill is unavailable. THE FIX, the developer's estimate: a small C# launcher compiled at runtime with PowerShell Add-Type. It calls CreateJobObject with KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE, creates the role process SUSPENDED, assigns it to the job, resumes it, relays the exit code and stdio (the prompt on stdin, the tails of stdout and stderr), and calls TerminateJobObject on the runtime's command. About 150-250 lines, plus 0.5-1.5s of PowerShell startup per stage. MUST FAIL CLOSED: Add-Type unavailable (constrained language mode) or AV interference refuses the loop and never falls back to an unkilled tree. PowerShell is a shell binary, so it may interpret only the runtime's fixed script and must pass the role's argv as data, never through a command line. CI is Linux, so only a Windows machine tests it; the row needs a Windows runner or states that limit. Residual it closes: R20's compare-then-call race on the generated config file, on the normal-exit path on Windows.

tasks.title: gitnexus-index measures distance in one direction only: an index on a different line of history reads as current
tasks.note: Found by the QA seat (Probe, record session 82) running sync --check twice in its tree, 2026-09-23; recorded in docs/loops/loop-15-slice-3-rulings-7.md. tasks.title: A seat started from a stale tree is briefed from STALE state: when the local record is older than origin/master's, ob_start renders the State block and the role files from origin/master (git show) and says so, so D-062 holds at every /start

PR #182 awaits merge' (merged 09-27), the handoff from session 74, and a role file without D-061. D-062 says the record reaches seats through origin/master; nothing makes a seat's /start READ master, so D-062 is defeated at every start from a stale tree. RULING: READ FROM MASTER, DO NOT REFUSE. A developer resuming on its own branch is legitimately behind master, and refusing to brief would block real work. tasks.title: A developer or QA seat's /start names its assignment, read from the record, or says 'no assignment' explicitly; it never stops at the backlog

Its T-194 r2 dispatch sat in a Cursor hub room it never reads, and nothing told the planner the seat existed. PROBLEM: an assignment exists only in a transport (hub turn or native A2A). Native A2A has no memory, and a message sent before the session exists never reaches it, so a fresh seat cannot find its work. OBSERVABLE GOAL: a fresh Claude Code developer or QA seat opened with a pending assignment starts on it with no human prompt. Mechanism is the developer's. It must read the record from origin/master when the tree is behind, so it is SEQUENCED AFTER T-200. Rows: a fixture with an assignment prints it, and one without prints 'no assignment'; a stale tree prints master's assignment, not the local one; a mutant that drops the assignment block goes red; the greeting-size check includes the block. RELATED, not duplicated: T-196 HB-3 and T-197 (the Cursor CLI side), T-199 (missing-handoff detection), T-191 (per-seat greeting profiles). tasks.title: A compute lease on the QA PC: a developer suite and SIA's qa-queue.ps1 each take one lease file before a run, so QA never starts over a developer suite and a developer suite never starts over QA; stale leases (expired, or owner process gone) are reclaimed
tasks.note: Opened planner session 150, 2026-09-30. Aaron approved the lease, relayed Aaron -> worktrees-d5 (Clark) -> Atlas, verbatim 'yes'. The ruling is the planner's. WHY: D-065 made the QA PC a developer machine first (pilot: Chisel, agent-dashboard), usable for SIA QA only when no developer suite runs; 'quiet' as a judgement is the thing that fails. SCOPE: (1) ONE helper script, tracked in SIA beside docs/loops/qa-queue.ps1 and copied to the QA PC's user folder the same way (never run from inside a checkout), with take / release / status. Other repos (agent-dashboard) call that copy; there are not two implementations. (2) The lease file lives outside every repo, in a fixed per-machine location, and holds {owner seat, session, pid, pid creation time, started, expires}. Taking it is ATOMIC (create-exclusive). (3) Stale-safe: a lease is reclaimable when expired, or when its pid is gone OR the pid's creation time differs (PID reuse; the gate Relay made binding for kills). (4) qa-queue.ps1 takes the lease for its whole run; while another live lease is held it waits and logs 'QA PC busy: <owner>' with a bounded wait, and never starts over it. (5) It fails closed: an unreadable or malformed lease file counts as HELD and says so, and is never silently ignored. ROWS: a held lease makes a queued QA wait and log the owner; a crashed holder (pid gone) is reclaimed, and so is a reused pid; two concurrent takers yield exactly one winner; a malformed file blocks with a named cause; a mutant with non-atomic take (check-then-write) loses the race row; a mutant that ignores the pid creation time loses the reuse row; the queue is red without the lease check and green with it. The queue-script change needs the machine copies re-copied (qa-launch.md). OUT OF SCOPE: agent-dashboard's own call site (Clark briefs Chisel once this exists). Seat: Forge, after T-203. Launch doc updated: the laptop is the default; the QA PC takes QA when the lease is free. — ADDED TO SCOPE, planner session 150 (QA 231's evidence): qa-queue.ps1 logged 'exit.231=0' and 'done_marker.231=True' for a run whose driver recorded complete=False and wrote no report (every attempt refused on a usage limit). The queue log reads as success while the driver knew it failed, which is the fail-open shape. Since T-204 edits qa-queue.ps1 anyway: the queue reads the driver's drive.meta 'complete=' line and logs 'complete.N=False (<reason>)' explicitly, and a model refusal or usage limit in run-*.err is named in the queue log. Row: a fixture driver meta with complete=False yields a complete.N=False line, never a bare done_marker=True. — PLAN RULED, planner session 150 (Forge on the QA PC, full plan to be committed as docs/loops/t204-plan.md on loop/t204-machine-lease): one machine-agnostic helper docs/loops/machine-lease.ps1 (take/release/status/renew), copied to %USERPROFILE% like qa-queue.ps1; lease file %USERPROFILE%\machine-lease\lease.json (per-user location ACCEPTED, with the limit printed in status output); atomic take by writing a temp file then Move-without-overwrite; the owner is a long-lived -OwnerPid plus its creation time; stale when expired, pid gone or pid creation time differing; unreadable or malformed means HELD (exit 11); release only by the owner. qa-queue.ps1 takes the lease after its own lock, waits bounded, aborts rather than running over a held lease, releases in finally, and logs complete.N and refusal_err.N (QA 231). The laptop's headless launch-qa.ps1 (Clark's) REFUSES when the lease is held, and takes it itself with -OwnerPid = the created claude pid; no release, since pid-gone reclaims it. That one line is Clark's change after T-204 merges. Rows R1-R10 with mutants (ignore creation time; check-then-write). Aaron re-copies both scripts per machine after the merge; the queue refuses without the lease copy. Branch prefix corrected from feat/ to loop/ (D-038). — BUILT, planner session 150 (Forge on the QA PC, Sonnet): loop/t204-machine-lease d5b3623 from master 066ed8c; plan docs/loops/t204-plan.md; handoff docs/loops/t204-developer-handoff.md. Harness docs/loops/machine-lease-harness.ps1: 24 rows pass on the candidate; all 7 queue rows are RED against master's qa-queue.ps1 (R8: a driver started over a live lease; R9b: a bare done_marker=True). Mutants are local (non-atomic take loses R5 30/30; ignoring the creation time loses R3; the queue without the lease loses R8/R8c). ACCEPTED ADDITION: the launcher makes TWO calls: take -OwnerPid $PID before creating the job (refusing on exit 10 or 11), then renew -NewOwnerPid <claude pid> right after Create (rows R7c/R7d). The exact lines for Clark are in t204-plan.md. ACCEPTED DEVIATION: queue -SelfTest lease checks dropped; the harness exercises the helper with real processes. NOT COVERED: vitest (no TS touched), anything on the laptop, and launch-qa.ps1 itself. QA not yet dispatched. After the merge, Aaron re-copies qa-queue.ps1 and machine-lease.ps1 on each machine (the queue refuses without the helper). tasks.title: A session start FETCHES before it judges currency: the SessionStart hook runs `git fetch --prune origin` (bounded timeout) before tree-currency and ob_start, says so visibly when it fails, and never calls a tree 'level' against a fetch it did not just make
tasks.note: Opened planner session 150, 2026-09-30, on Aaron's approval ('send it to Atlas to rule on', relayed Aaron -> clark -> Atlas). EVIDENCE, two stale-fetch misreads within about an hour: (1) the planner read the T-207 probe ref as undeleted from an unpruned remote-tracking ref (rev 196's correction); (2) Forge's /start on the QA PC printed 'HEAD 9c603615, level with origin/master, state rev 178 level with origin/master rev 178' while origin/master was at about rev 194 (#221 7c925a6, #222 cdf079d, including Forge's own rev-183 handoff). ob_start compares against the LAST fetch and says so, but nothing makes the fetch happen, so T-200's 'brief from master' is only as fresh as a fetch nobody ran, and D-062 is defeated at /start again. RULING: DETERMINISTIC, not a prompt step. The SessionStart hook (cli-bootstrap), which already prints tree currency, runs `git fetch --prune origin` FIRST, with a bounded timeout (network), then computes currency. On failure it prints 'fetch FAILED: <cause>; currency is against a fetch from <time>' and the currency line never says 'level' unqualified. ob_start states the fetch time it compared against. The /start command text gets no fetch step, because the hook owns it. ROWS: a fixture with an origin that moved after the last fetch: before the change it reads 'level' (red), after it reads 'behind' (green); an unreachable origin prints the FAILED line and the old fetch time; the fetch is bounded (a hanging remote does not hang /start); a mutant that skips the fetch goes red on the first row; prune is proven (a deleted remote branch is gone after start). NOT THIS TASK: the Cursor copy (T-197 parity follows it). SEQUENCED AFTER T-200 merges (it touches tree-currency, which T-200 also changed). Seat: builder (it built T-200's record source and knows tree-currency). — ACCEPTANCE ROW ADDED, planner session 153 (resumed after a desktop reboot), 2026-10-01, on clark's restart audit (hoh-startup-audit.md): 'fires on SessionStart resume as well as startup, and prints tree currency and drift in one line'. WHY: the planner resumed after hours of downtime. The SessionStart:resume hook did fire and print tree currency (against the last fetch), but nothing ran a fresh fetch or the drift check. The planner fetched by hand (06:28Z) and ran the drift check only when asked: ob_start at 06:3x showed 'Drift: none', level with origin/master rev 222, session log reused. T-208's ruling named 'the SessionStart hook' without naming the event, so resume was implied but not pinned.

gaps.what: One session uuid is written under two different project keys in active-session.json, corrupting project-scoped attribution.
gaps.evidence: Live slot file: uuid d7e514f8-df2a-483c-a8c7-57f2e0a931b0 appears under BOTH 'c:/users/melve/appdata/roaming/cura/5.10/definition_changes::claude' (started_at 2026-09-08T01:39:45Z) and 'c:/users/melve/.claude/projects/c--users-melve/memory::claude' (started_at 2026-09-09T02:01:03Z). Mechanism established from source, not guessed: cli-bootstrap.ts writes the slot under activeSessionKey(canonicalizeProjectDir(cwd), ide) on every SessionStart invocation, and writeActiveSession (shared/active-session.ts) merges into the file by key - it never removes an existing key holding the same uuid. So a session that starts (or resumes) under a second directory gains a second key pointing at one uuid, and both keys then read back as live. Note the two source comments disagree about whether this can happen: cli-bootstrap.ts says 'this hook runs exactly once per session' while active-session.ts says 'every session start - including a resume - rewrites the slot'. Which trigger produced THIS pair is not recoverable: the SessionStart payload carries a 'source' field distinguishing startup/resume/clear, and the slot records payload key NAMES only, never values - the same drop-your-input defect describeWorkspaceDir was written to fix. This is the INVERSE of T-003: T-003 is two sessions sharing one identity, this is one session claiming two projects. T-003's guards (resolveWriteSession preferring the in-memory id, STALE_SESSION_MS refusing old slots) do not address it, because both keys are fresh and both are genuinely this session's uuid. It matters because every measurement in the Loop 7 C1 reconciliation is attributed by session uuid and scoped by project.
gaps.recommended_update: Decide whether a uuid may hold more than one project key at all. If not, writeActiveSession should evict any other key carrying the same uuid before inserting. Either way, store the SessionStart 'source' VALUE in the entry so the trigger is readable next time instead of re-derived.

gaps.what: expected_revision serialises writes within one lineage, not across branches. decisions.title: Amendment vocabulary: which state records can be corrected, and which are append-only
decisions.note:
Decided once rather than one op per incident. The op union grew by accident — update_task exists because someone needed it, update_gap did not because nobody had yet — and Loop 5 hit the consequence twice in one night.

RULE: a record is amendable when its text DESCRIBES SOMETHING STILL BEING LEARNED. A record is append-only when its text IS THE HISTORICAL FACT, so that editing it destroys the thing the record exists to preserve.

Per type:
- TASKS — amendable (open/update/close/reopen). Title and priority are current intent, which legitimately changes. Already correct.
- GAPS — amendable. A gap describes something we do not yet understand, so its text is provisional by construction. The record most needing correction was the one that could not be corrected. IMPLEMENTED this loop: update_gap. The prior workaround (close + re-add) silently minted a new id and reset opened_session, losing the history the gap list exists to keep.
- VERIFIED — claim append-only; evidence appends; status reopens. The claim is what evidence was gathered against, so editing it invalidates that evidence silently while leaving it attached. Already correct; no update_verified.
- DECISIONS — append-only. A decision log records what was decided and when; amending it is not a correction but a rewrite of the record. Supersede with a new decision instead. Already correct; no update_decision. Gap: decisions carry no supersedes field (tasks do), so superseding is convention only.
- OBJECTIVE / HANDOFF / LAST_SESSION — singletons, set wholesale. Already correct.
- PROJECT.VERSION — REMOVE; do not add set_version. No consumer treats it as authoritative: cli.ts:427 and session-start/state-render.ts:14 display it, state-import/index.ts:439,494 copy it, drift-detector.ts:9 + checks-state.ts:73 + checks.ts:783 compare it to package.json and complain, and state-writer.ts:166 prefers package.json with this only as fallback. It is a cached copy of a truth held elsewhere, with a drift branch and two checks existing solely to police the cache. DEFERRED to Loop 7: 7 call sites plus schema, a state.json migration and test updates is larger than the decision.

ID SCHEME, observed while filing this: the Planner's brief assumed the next ADR id was free, but ADR-021..ADR-026 already exist and nextId has since minted D-001..D-003 alongside them, so the list now carries both schemes. This decision took an explicit ADR-027 to avoid widening the split. The generation bug itself stays filed under G-005 — it is an id question, not an amendment one.

decisions.title: No ranking constant changes on one measured alternative beating one incumbent
decisions.note:
Loop 6's repaired instrument made the recency question answerable and recency_strong (0.02/day) was the only strategy to beat live — 21-11-5, +0.0153 nDCG, winning against a presentation bias that favours the incumbent. The constant was still NOT changed.

Reasoning: recency_strong tests ONE alternative point against ONE incumbent. That 0.02 beats 0.005 is evidence the constant is too low. It is not evidence that 0.02 is right — nothing between or beyond was measured, and the optimum could be anywhere above 0.005. Adopting the one other number that happened to be guessed in the strategy list is the 'flipped because the new number is bigger' outcome the loop's own precondition rules out, and it rules it out whether or not the bigger number won.

shadow/index.ts states the same contract independently: changing production constants stays a human decision; the harness only supplies the evidence. The evidence is now worth supplying, which it was not before this loop.

Recommended next measurement: a sweep — 0.01 / 0.02 / 0.04 as separate strategies — to find where the gain turns over. Adoption is Aaron's call.

What the same run did NOT license: no_maturity ties live, and that must not be read as 'maturity boosts are harmless'. See G-013 (feedback_log 31% complete) and G-014 (success_rate ignores neutral).

decisions.title: ADR-029 - Keep session-start retrieval; suspend the maturity lifecycle; leave the causal question unasked
decisions.note: Loop 7's deliverable, RECOMMENDED not yet adopted - Aaron rules (T-129). 'Does injection earn its place' was three questions wearing one coat, and bundling them is what nearly retired the cheap half on evidence that only ever concerned the expensive half. STEM Agent's argument is that a maturation lifecycle belongs on an EXECUTABLE unit because only an execution yields an objective outcome; that indicts success_rate, maturity and apoptosis on knowledge entries and says nothing about whether fetching a note is worthwhile. A bookmark is not improved by a promotion ladder. Keep retrieval: the case against it was a claim retracted in the vault 26 minutes after it was written, and the first adequately powered contrast this project has produced runs in its favour (start 0.337 vs explicit 0.259 per-entry, n=109 and n=56, opposite to the pre-registration's own selection-bias prediction). Per prereg §5 that is not evidence injection helps - it refutes the claim that injection is the low-value mode. Suspend the lifecycle: success_rate is near-two-valued (98% of rated entries read exactly 1.0), apoptosis cannot fire on arithmetic (needs >=4 harmful on one entry, observed max 1), no_maturity tied live in Loop 6, and the ladder is a ratchet. Recency decay by contrast IS validated, so this is not 'ranking is worthless'. The causal question: control arm named concretely (randomised withhold flag in sessions at ob_start plus a non-self-reported outcome) and then argued against on the pre-registration's own costing - at ~2 sessions/week no effect smaller than enormous is resolvable.

decisions.title: ADR-030 - A bug fix that revives a dead code path ships gated off
decisions.note: Correcting the session-uuid bug in cli-session-end.ts would have switched the dormant heuristic rating arm on at the next session end, feeding topic-mention signal into a scoring system whose per-entry mean (0.311) sits one hundredth above its apoptosis threshold (0.3) - during the very loop deciding whether to keep that system. So the repair and the switch-on ship as two separable things: enableHeuristicRatings defaults false, and the doc comment carries the argument so whoever flips it later sees it rather than re-deriving it. Rows produced after the fix are out of sample for Loop 7, the population having been fixed before the change. Secondary rule, and the part that was nearly missed: with the gate closed an unjudged entry is SKIPPED, not recorded neutral - a fallback neutral is indistinguishable from a rater's considered 'retrieved and not used', so the cheaper diff would have destroyed the only signal the corpus still has while appearing to strengthen the data.

The upper bound is CLAUDE.md: injected at 100% delivery, top of context, every session, carrying the sentence that the summaries table does not exist, while /start instructed agents to call ob_summarize() and ob_store_summary() which do not exist and command-parity reported pass. decisions.title: ADR-029 (D-004) adopted as written - the record catching up to code that has run under it for three loops
decisions.note: Aaron adopted it on 2026-09-17, asked directly and answered directly. D-004 had stood as 'RECOMMENDED not yet adopted - Aaron rules (T-129)' since 2026-09-15. It was never a pending direction: Loops 8, 10 and 11 implemented all of it. matureBoost and provenBoost are 1.0, the apoptosis gate is off, the maturity lifecycle and success_rate are cut, session-start retrieval is kept. THE CODE HAD BEEN LIVING UNDER THIS DECISION FOR THREE LOOPS WHILE THE RECORD SAID NOBODY HAD MADE IT - which is Loop 11's defect class arriving in the decision log rather than in prose: a record describing a state the system had already left. Recorded as its own decision rather than by editing D-004, because ob_state has no update_decision op and because the sequence is worth keeping: recommended 2026-09-15, implemented across three loops, formally adopted 2026-09-17. NOT DECIDED BY THIS: whether the suspension should ever be reversed - D-004's own trigger language stands - and the $declined retirement of success_rate, Maturity and Rating, which Aaron deferred to Loop 13 on the same day. The behaviour is cut; the vocabulary and the column are not, and recording that as finished would make the retirements check green on an unfinished cut.

decisions.title: Retire the agent mailbox - SIA channel only
decisions.note: Aaron: 'the mailbox was pre-A2A and should be retired. HoH with A2A solves the agent-to-agent communication issue', scoped on ruling to the sia channel alone. ~/.agents/mailbox/ served NINE channels, eight non-empty, and seven belong to other projects (nexcrm has three named seats; worthit and TCM were missed in the first enumeration because it was read off a truncated `head -25`). The brief's framing 'decisions -> state.json decisions[]' was WRONG - the mailbox log holds 67 entries from 2026-04-16 and state.json holds 43 from 2026-03-22, two different records that overlap without matching.

decisions.title: Forge may publish its own loop branches
decisions.note: Aaron, resolving an inconsistency the Planner surfaced rather than used: Loop 11's Developer pushed loop/11-instructions and opened PR #18 under what it believed were the same instructions, while Forge held a standing 'tag, never push'. One instruction, two readings, a whole loop apart. Forge pushes and opens the PR; the Planner tags the merge commit on master. Loop 12 cost a few hours of an unopened PR because Forge declined to publish on a peer's say-so and then declined again on a relay of Aaron's answer, confirming with Aaron directly instead. Recorded as the right price rather than an over-caution: a peer cannot extend reserved authority, and a relay of an answer is still the same channel.

decisions.title: ADR-031 - a sign-off transfers across an amend only when the amend is provably disjoint
decisions.note: Refines 'a sign-off does not transfer across an amend', which made every post-QA prose fix cost a re-QA and therefore made the cheap path be not fixing prose, or amending quietly. New rule: it transfers when the amend is provably disjoint from what was signed, and PROVABLY MEANS A DIFF THE QA SEAT CAN RUN - in practice `git diff --stat <signed-sha> HEAD -- <executable paths>` handed over showing empty. Paired with the error-table admission rule: the table records a wrong claim that reached an artifact, a commit, a counterpart or Aaron; a near-miss caught in-process by its own author goes in a separate register as an instance of a named family, never numbered. THE DIVIDING LINE IS ESCAPE, NOT SEVERITY. Both rules exist to stop a correctness rule taxing the behaviour it wants - a rule that adds a row every time someone checks their own work makes checking your own work look like failure. Requested by the seat that stood to benefit from the looser rule, after noticing it had already drafted the entry before asking.

decisions.title: Loop 13 is Idea B - the module boundary
decisions.note: Aaron ruled, against the alternative of G-026 (recall precision), which he had earlier pencilled in. The Planner argued for Idea B and not on the grounds that it was owed a turn: G-026's urgency is contingent on recall being USED, and three consecutive loops have now run with zero recalls, so tuning precision on a system nobody queries optimises a thing whose value is unestablished. Idea B - core installable with Node and git, memory an opt-in module - is the instrument for the question open since Loop 9: not 'does injection change behaviour', which Loop 10 answered, but 'does the memory half get used at all'. Idea B had been scheduled as Loop 7 and displaced four times, every time into a loop that had its own subject, by the sentence 'it fits cleanly with what we are already touching' - a sentence the Planner itself wrote about the lifecycle cut four hours before quoting the pattern back.

decisions.title: Loop 13's C4 closes as a recorded failure
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat (Atlas), 2026-09-17, in the words 'yes, Loop 13's C4 closes as a recorded failure'. C4 asked whether core installs and runs with Node and git alone, memory absent. It does NOT, and the reason is the finding: THE MACHINERY IS INSTALLABLE; THE INSTRUCTION IS NOT. Forge ran a real install - fresh clone, npm install --omit=optional, better-sqlite3 confirmed ABSENT before anything ran, env vars pointed at nonexistent paths - and everything mechanical passed: install, build, sync --check (21 passed, 4 skipped, the three memory checks SKIPPING WITH THE REASON rather than passing), open-brain start exit 0, cli-bootstrap.js exit 0 with project detected and agent identity read. server.js died correctly, because it IS the memory half. The loop fails at the instruction layer only. Aaron ruled ONLY that the command surface and hook installation are not Loop 13's work. He did NOT rule them as the next loop's subject; that is recorded as an open task with its derivation, not as a decision. A loop that ends in an honest no is not a failed loop, and the brief was written to make this outcome reportable: it either passes or it does not, and there is no partial credit to hide in.

decisions.title: The HoH loop is autonomous inside a branch; Aaron holds master until the shadow-gate count says otherwise
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat, by returning the planner's recommendation verbatim: 'autonomous inside a branch, you at master, with the runtime recording what it would have done at each merge so your disagreements become a count. The day that count is zero across loops with real defects in them, remove the gate on evidence.' THIS RESOLVES THE CONFLICT RECORDED IN docs/HOH-JEV.md §6.2 AND docs/loops/loop-15-brief.md §5.1: hoh_jev.md specified a loop that never blocks on a human, which was incompatible with 'Aaron merges, on his word', a rule that has held for every loop in this record. WHAT IS AUTONOMOUS: the plan gate, the developer done-gate, QA scoring, retry, and rollback — closed questions with criteria written in advance, run by the runtime without a human. WHAT IS NOT: the merge to master. The runtime stops at a candidate commit and never merges, pushes to master, or tags. WHY THE MERGE STAYS HUMAN, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN NERVES: every serious defect found recently passed the automated checks and was caught by a human question or a human-ordered real run — the retirements check green through five merged PRs then 115 findings in the main tree; build-freshness shipped with its author's tests green and wrong in two checkouts of three; the main tree fifteen commits stale and reporting pass. A gate is a calibrated judge of the evidence it is shown, and every one of those failures was in the evidence, not the judgement. TypeSafe's own words: typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. THE EXIT CRITERION IS MEASURABLE: the runtime records, at every merge decision, what it WOULD have done. Aaron still merges. Each time his decision differs from the runtime's is counted. When that count is zero across several loops that contained real defects, the human gate is redundant and is removed — on evidence. If it is not zero, the count is exactly what would have been lost. This is 'see it red before you trust it green' applied to the human gate itself. WHAT NO GATE REPLACES, stated so it is not quietly automated later: asking the question nobody wrote down. Jev answers questions it is asked; the observation that Loop 14 was briefed against a world that no longer existed came from a person noticing, not from a gate.

decisions.title: D-020 — the HoH runtime lives at open-brain/src/harness/, not the repo root
decisions.note: The brief writes `harness/`. The same reasoning that ruled TypeScript over Python — one build, one test command, one CI lane — applies to a second root-level project. The deciding factor was that module-boundary reads only open-brain/src: at the repo root the runtime whose entire job is enforcing a boundary would have sat outside the only check that asserts the dependency direction. Inside, it is checked as core, passes, and a future import of memory would fail /sync.

decisions.title: D-021 — zod is the deliverable-schema source; the .schema.json files are derived and drift-checked
decisions.note: A hand-maintained JSON Schema beside a runtime validator is two statements of one shape, which is the defect family most of this record is made of. schema.test.ts regenerates from zod and compares byte for byte; seen red on a hand-edited minLength. The two rules JSON Schema cannot express — new_capability non-empty unless stop_ship is requested and justified, repair_targets non-empty — are written into the generated files' own description, so a reader validating against the file alone is told what it cannot see. Regenerate with `npx tsx src/harness/cli.ts schemas --write`; it refuses to write into a build directory.

decisions.title: D-028 — A2A-Hub on tcm is the seats' chatter transport; the record stays in tracked files
decisions.note: Claude Code cross-session discovery returned nobody on this machine (three sessions, bound inbox pipes, valid keys, v2.1.278; feedback drafted). Deployed A2A-Hub to tcm (100.124.212.87:4000, Tailscale) on Aaron's word and ran Loop 16 on it. Rules learned, all from failures: the read cursor moves only on a read (two turns were dropped on a send before Clark's fix c85c0d3); one background listener per seat, re-armed only after the previous exits; every hub message from a file (an inline backtick is a command substitution); the wake is the harness re-invoking a session when its background `hub-talk --wait` exits — measured on both paths. Silence on this transport is still ambiguous ('no messages' vs 'no listener') — T-160. AUTH_MODE stays warn until per-agent keys exist.

decisions.title: Seats on one machine use native cross-session messaging; A2A-Hub is for cross-machine
decisions.note: AMENDS D-028, whose premise was that Claude Code cross-session discovery is broken on this machine. That premise is FALSE and was tested end to end on 2026-09-21 with three live seats (planner sia-planner-1c, developer sia-forge-42, QA sia-qa-24). All six directions were attested BY THE RECEIVING SIDE, never by a send receipt: both seats independently refused to treat success:true as delivery. An idle seat wakes on inbound with no human in the path — measured at 1.486s from receipt to first tool call. The queue-hold hypothesis is excluded by MAGNITUDE (|delta| = 227ms between the sender's success return and the receiver's context receipt, against the seconds-to-minutes a human-gated hold predicts), which does not require trusting two processes' log clocks at sub-second resolution; the ordering (delivery BEFORE the sender's own acknowledgment) is suggestive but not load-bearing. D-028's hub deployment keeps its role for CROSS-MACHINE traffic and for the Grok bot; it is no longer the default for seats on one box. Known limit, from the QA seat: ListAgents has a registration lag — the developer's listing showed only the planner while the QA seat was already running, and an early or short listing is INDISTINGUISHABLE from a seat that is not running. Nothing may gate on a single ListAgents poll.

decisions.title: SIA reaches a working point on Claude Code first; Cursor is bridged afterwards through A2A-Hub, at close-to-parity rather than 1:1
decisions.note: AARON'S SEQUENCING, stated at the close of session 77 and recorded because it was about to exist only in a chat. PHASE 1: get SIA to a good working point on Claude Code. PHASE 2: bring Cursor in through A2A-Hub. PARITY IS EXPLICITLY NOT THE TARGET - 'maybe not 1 to 1 parity but close'. A Cursor seat needs enough to BE A SEAT, not every SIA feature, and that scope call belongs to phase 2 rather than being assumed now. THIS AMENDS D-029's SCOPE. D-029 ruled native cross-session messaging for seats on one machine and the hub for CROSS-MACHINE traffic. A Cursor seat is neither: it sits on the same box and cannot speak Claude Code's native cross-session protocol at all, since ListAgents/SendMessage are host features rather than anything this repo controls. So the hub's role is CROSS-MACHINE AND CROSS-HARNESS, and a same-box Cursor seat is the second case. Native stays the default only between Claude Code seats. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR PRIORITY, because the planner raised T-046 to P0 one revision earlier on the idle-meter argument: T-046, G-001 and G-009 gate PHASE 2, not slice three. They stay P0 as the gate on a whole phase and on capacity already paid for (Cursor Pro+ $60/month, Cursor Models 7% used, Other Models 0%, resets Oct 3), but they are NOT work that interrupts the current loop. The planner's idle-meter framing was an argument about value, not about sequence; Aaron supplied the sequence. STILL TO ESTABLISH BEFORE PHASE 2 IS PLANNED, and not assumed here: which Cursor pool a given model draws from - Other Models spills to on-demand spend, which is disabled, so '0% used' is not 'any model runs free'. And whether a hub-bridged Cursor seat can meet the loop's evidence rules at all: frozen SHA, exit-code-only verdicts, and a write allowlist the runtime enforces are Claude-Code-side today.

decisions.title: A loop candidate carries no version bump; the bump and CHANGELOG entry go in a separate release commit after QA acceptance
decisions.note: AARON'S RULING, session 78 ('release commit after acceptance'), answering the question open since session 77. The candidate QA scores is exactly the candidate that merges: no commit is added to it between acceptance and merge except the release commit, and that one touches only package.json, CHANGELOG.md and the version surfaces /sync keeps consistent. The QA seat confirms its diff touches no source or test, as V-059 did for 3135da4 in Loop 14. FOR LOOP CANDIDATES THIS OVERRIDES the global CLAUDE.md rule 'bump at commit time'; outside a loop (chore, docs, hotfix) the global rule stands. decisions.title: Standing merge authority for record/docs-only PRs; Aaron keeps the merge for loop candidates and anything touching code, instructions or checks
decisions.note: AARON'S RULING, session 78 ('I've approved every merge, do we really need that check from me?', then 'yes' to the planner's proposal). AMENDS the shared.md line 'Aaron merges, on his word' FOR ONE CLASS OF PR ONLY. COVERED: a PR whose EVERY changed path is in this allowlist: docs/** ; README.md ; .agents/state.json ; its four rendered views (.agents/TASKS/INBOX.md, .agents/TASKS/task.md, .agents/SESSIONS/next-session.md, .agents/SYSTEM/SUMMARY.md) ; the scope layer (.agents/SYSTEM/PRD.md, DECISIONS.md, ENTITIES.md). Any seat may merge such a PR when ALL of these hold: CI conclusion success; mergeStateStatus CLEAN (UNKNOWN and UNSTABLE mean not yet); the merge pinned with --match-head-commit to the SHA the conditions were read at; and the merge verified against origin/master afterwards, not taken from the command's exit code. NOT COVERED, still Aaron's word: loop candidates; anything under open-brain/ (source, tests, build config); hooks; package.json and CHANGELOG.md (the release commit, D-031); .claude/ (commands); .agents/roles/, .agents/SYSTEM/RULES.md and the rest of the operating layer; .agents/retirements.json and any other data a check reads. Those change how seats behave or what a check enforces. WHY THE LINE IS THERE: (1) Aaron's merge decision on a candidate is the ground truth T-155's shadow gate counts against, and an agent merging would make it count disagreements with another agent; (2) a code merge is release to consumers (D-019: autonomous inside a branch, Aaron at master). THE CHECK IS PATH-BASED AND MECHANICAL, NOT A JUDGEMENT: until it is a script, the merging seat runs `gh pr diff <n> --name-only`, tests every path against the allowlist, and puts the list and the result in a PR comment BEFORE merging. A single unlisted path sends the PR to Aaron. SIZE IS NOT A CRITERION. A large record PR is covered, and a one-line change to a role file is not. A seat in doubt sends it to Aaron. The first PR under this authority is the one that records it. Aaron's 'yes' is to this text, and the PR says so.

decisions.title: Other projects' seats on this machine work normally and are RECORDED beside SIA suite results; they pause only when a SIA seat requests a controlled rerun

decisions.title: Seats start FRESH SESSIONS at each candidate boundary; the handoff between them is tracked files, never a long-running context
decisions.note: AARON'S RULING, session 78 ('yes'), raised by his observation that the developer seat was at about 28% context and the QA seat nearly as low partway through candidate A. Context belongs to a SESSION, not a loop; a loop runs out of it only when one session carries several candidates. RULE: after QA's verdict on a candidate, the developer and QA seats write their tracked handoff (the developer report, the QA report, design files) and stop; fresh sessions take the next candidate from tracked files (brief, rulings, criteria, reports), re-read at full context. They do not /end until T-163 lands. Anything that exists only in a seat's context at the boundary must be moved into a tracked file first. COROLLARY, from candidate A's cost: the max-effort criteria re-read and the rulings it produces come BEFORE the build starts, not during it. Candidate A grew from 5 rulings to 22 mid-build, and every late ruling cost context in two seats.

decisions.title: AMENDS D-033: slice three closes at candidates A, B and C. B = the G-042 repair plus E_t's schema change; C = T-155's shadow merge gate
decisions.note: AARON'S RULING, session 78 ('yes'). Decisions are add-only (G-010), so this amends D-033 rather than editing it. B was ruled as G-042's repair (rulings-5 R23) plus all of T-155. The developer's B-repair design alone (load generator, eld instrument, stage-boundary yields, async execFile in cli.test.ts, AST sweep, optional vitest projects split) is substantial, and T-155 (verdict function, merge.json policy, shadow-verdict CLI, derived decision, append-only ledger, /sync check, retrospective backfill) is at least as large, so one candidate would have been roughly candidate A's size again. SPLIT: B = the G-042 repair (design at loop/15-slice-3-forge-design-b e1173b1, Step 0 first per the planner's ruling) + E_t's schema change (rulings-2 R10); C = T-155, built on B's accepted SHA. Each gets its own criteria before its candidate. Jev calibration stays the next slice (D-033).

decisions.title: Memory is LOOKUP by default and INJECTION only on a deterministic match against the act; the fix starts on the WRITE side (T-170 adopted)
decisions.note: AARON'S RULING, session 78 ('T-170 looks correct'). Adopts T-170's recommendation as the memory layer's direction. (a) Where the agent knows it needs something, memory is a LOOKUP: ob_recall with trigger 'explicit'. Evidence: Loop 10's p=0.688 for session-start injection once topic-matched; CLAUDE.md, delivered at 100% reliability, not changing behaviour; HoH's gains with no memory module. (b) Where the agent cannot know to ask (G-039's case, and the PRD's 'lessons from past mistakes are forgotten'), memory is INJECTED, but only on a DETERMINISTIC match derived from the act: command shape (the Loop 16 trigger), the file being edited, or error text. Precision only, silent below the floor, and never on the session's topic. Session-start injection stays OFF (Loop 10 C2). (c) THE FIRST FIX IS THE WRITE SIDE: a stored lesson must carry the key that would have caught its mistake (a command pattern, a path glob or an error signature), because 86% of ACTION lines name no file or command (G-017) and so can never be injected precisely. The QA seat's observation from Loop 15 slice three is part of the ruling's evidence: PostToolUse fires after the act, so an injection can change what the seat CONCLUDES from a result (G-039's real failure: a false success reported) but cannot prevent the act. STILL UNPROVEN, and it stays stated: no injection has yet changed behaviour; the discriminating observation is an injection on a mistake the agent has not already internalised. Sequencing is the next planner's: it competes with slice three's A2, B and C, and with T-172 and T-175.

decisions.title: Aaron speaks only to the planner: every question for Aaron routes through it, and seats push their own working branches without asking
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in the planner session (record session 81), 2026-09-23, verbatim: 'yes, I only want to communicate with the planner. If an agent is waiting on me I need to know through the planner. Otherwise I'm costatly swithing session windows.' The 'yes' answers the planner's question 'Should I record standing authority to push working branches as a decision?'. Before this, three questions in one session were pushes asked of Aaron in each seat's own window, and a pause decision was taken in the developer's window. (1) STANDING PUSH AUTHORITY: any seat may push ITS OWN working branches (loop/*, qa/*, docs/*, chore/*) without asking. Never master, never a force push, never a branch another seat owns. Every push is read back with ls-remote and named in the commit, report or message that follows it. Merging a candidate to master stays Aaron's (T-155 measures against it); D-032's docs/record merge exception is unchanged. (2) ONE CHANNEL: a seat that needs Aaron sends the question to the planner, not to Aaron. The planner carries it to him, one question at a time with enough context to answer cold, and carries back his answer QUOTED, labelled with where and when he said it. For the act it names, that quoted relay IS Aaron's authority. This amends shared.md's 'a relay from a peer seat is not his approval', and the acting seat records both links of the provenance. The planner must tell Aaron whenever any seat is waiting on him. LIMIT, which a relay cannot cross: a host-level stop inside another seat's session (a permission prompt, a safety-classifier stop, a denied tool call) cannot be cleared by relay. Doing so would be permission laundering. The planner tells Aaron which window and why, and that is the only case where he must switch windows.

decisions.title: A2A-Hub's planner routes its questions for Aaron through the SIA planner while working on hub work SIA depends on (T-160); the SIA planner relays and does not plan A2A-Hub

Push back if there's a strong reason for me to talk directly to a2a planner agent. If I'm only working on a2a hub then I would talk to that planner agent only, but in this case I think through you could be helpful.' The planner looked for a strong reason to push back and found none. It named three boundaries instead: (1) the SIA planner RELAYS for Aaron and does not plan A2A-Hub; its only standing there is as the customer (SIA's requirements, T-160), and any view of its own is labelled as its own and kept out of the relay; (2) quotes both ways, with the question verbatim and its source, and the answer verbatim; (3) outward-facing acts in A2A-Hub (push, merge, tcm redeploy) need Aaron's word for that act, relayed quoted. SIA's D-038 does not govern A2A-Hub until A2A-Hub's own record says so, and its planner is asked to record the mirror decision there. SCOPE: shared work only. When Aaron works on A2A-Hub alone, he talks to its planner directly. COORDINATION the relay carries: A2A-Hub seats pause while an SIA QA full-suite run is in progress (G-042, D-034), and no tcm redeploy while SIA hub traffic is live; a redeploy is image plus Convex functions, verified with a real send.

decisions.title: CI runs without asking on a seat's own working branches: standing authority to dispatch now, an automatic trigger to follow (T-178)
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in the SIA planner session (record session 90), 2026-09-23, verbatim: 'ci should run autonoumously'. Said just after he authorised QA 89's one workflow_dispatch on qa/loop-15-slice-3-a4-probe (run 35928008495), the first time a seat had to ask for a CI run. The planner's interpretation, recorded as its own and open to his correction: CI on a seat's working branch is not an act that needs a per-occasion word. TWO PARTS. (1) STANDING NOW: any seat may dispatch or re-run CI (gh workflow run CI --ref <branch>, gh run rerun) on a branch it owns under D-038 (loop/*, qa/*, docs/*, chore/*) without asking, and names the run id in the report or message that follows. It never covers master or another seat's branch, and it grants nothing else: pushing to master, merging, tagging and editing workflows stay where D-032/D-038 put them. (2) STRUCTURAL, so nobody has to remember to dispatch: T-178 makes ci.yml trigger on push to those branch prefixes. ci.yml is not on D-032's allowlist, so that change is a PR Aaron merges. WHY THE LINE IS WHERE IT IS: a CI run on a private repo changes no branch, cannot alter a candidate, and runs off this machine, so it adds no local load (G-042). Its only cost is Actions minutes. Until now the ci.yml triggers (push to master, pull_request, workflow_dispatch) meant a working branch without a PR could only be tested on Linux by asking, and QA 89's predicted POSIX-only R49 sibling showed what that costs: a prediction that cannot fail a row until someone asks for the instrument.

decisions.title: Candidate A6 changes approach: the operating system resolves links and the runtime compares only which file it reaches (same object = read, different = report, unresolvable = report as unwatched); CA-15 clause 3 is amended BEFORE A6 is built
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in the SIA planner session (record session 90), 2026-09-24 ~04:00Z, verbatim: 'yes, let's do it for a6.' He was answering the planner's question: 'Should candidate A's rule become "read only the same file that was there at base, confirmed by the operating system", with CA-15 clause 3 amended before A6 is built?' WHY: candidate A has been through six rounds on CA-15 (A to A5). Every defect since A2 came from hand-written route tracing (R43/R44/R49/R55 and their builds), and A5-1 (QA 92 interim, measured on Linux CI 35952428545 against A4 35952430721) is that tracing silently dropping stow, relative and multi-level folder links from watch. WHAT A6 DOES (the planner's statement of the result; the mechanism is the developer's): at base, each machine-config path is resolved by the OS to its real file, and that file's identity (type, dev, ino, nlink) is recorded. A path that does not resolve is reported at base as UNWATCHED, never silently. After a stage: resolve again. Same file: open it, confirm by fstat on the opened handle that it is still that file, and only then read. This closes the R37 check-then-read race, until now a named limit. Different file: do not read; report the path with its base and current resolution. A link planted AT the watched path itself is still reported (A4's lexical check). The hand-written route walk (routeChain) is removed. THE TRADE, stated so nobody inherits it as settled: a newly planted link that leads to the SAME base file will be read. That file was already allowed (clause 3's first bullet: reads confined to the machine-config paths as they stood at base), so nothing outside is exposed, but clause 3's second bullet ('not read THROUGH a link ... not there at base') changes meaning. CRITERIA DISCIPLINE: this is a criteria amendment made BEFORE any A6 candidate exists, on the merits and on Aaron's word. It is not a widening after a verdict. It is written into the criteria file (or a numbered ruling the criteria cite) before the A6 brief, with a read-back of every row it touches. QA 92's verdict on A5 is unaffected and is scored against the criteria as they stood.

decisions.title: R67 approved: the machine-config read gate is 'same place, not shared' (same real path, and either the base file ignoring nlink or a regular file with exactly one name), re-checked on the opened handle; this amends D-041's 'same file as at base'
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in the SIA planner session (record session 90), 2026-09-24 ~19:57Z, verbatim: 'sounds right'. He was answering the planner's question: 'Should the rule become "same place, not shared"? The runtime would read the file if it is at the same real path and is either the original file or a new file with no other names. That keeps the protection: a redirected link, or a file shared with something outside, is still never read. I recommend yes. The trade: a file replaced at the same spot gets read, and its contents are ones the agent could have written into the original file anyway.' WHY: QA report A6 (ea825b7) §11.1 and §11.5, and A6-1. Under D-041's 'same file', `git config --global` (lock+rename, a new inode) and editors that save by replacing the file made CA-4f's ordinary write unhashable, and nlink in the identity flipped a path to not-read whenever a hard link was made anywhere. THE RULE (rulings-14 R67): after preflight, read a machine-config path only if (1) realpath equals the base realpath, and (2) the file there is the base file (dev, ino and type; nlink excluded) OR a regular file with nlink 1. Both are re-checked on the opened handle before any byte is read. Anything else is not read and is reported with both resolutions and identities. THE TRADE, recorded: QA 89's A4-1 R shape (the base target replaced by a new file) becomes READ. A4-1's H, J and LOOP stay unread. Nothing is read through a redirection or from a file with another name. Criteria discipline: amended before any A7 candidate exists, on Aaron's word.

watch_out: CLOSED GAP IDS ARE HANDED BACK BY THE NEXT add_gap. At rev 60 a dry run assigned G-046 and G-047 — ids closed at rev 59 whose OLD meanings are cited in ten tracked files, including .claude/commands/end.md, which explains the per-seat handoff by citing G-046. Done-task retention now protects ids the tree cites (it KEPT T-157 in this very write, with a NOTE); gaps have no such guard, and the gap failure is worse: an evicted task id goes DANGLING and announces itself, while a reused gap id points at something WRONG and does not. DRY RUN EVERY add_gap AND CHECK THE ASSIGNED ID AGAINST `git grep` BEFORE THE REAL CALL.

ob_stats SHOWING `hook: 1` IS NOT EVIDENCE THE SERVER KNOWS ABOUT THE TRIGGER. That census is a GROUP BY over recall_log values, so a stale build prints it from data alone. The three fire counts from trigger_fires are the discriminator, and the planner's check was worded to require them — one word looser and a pre-0.44.0 server would have been declared current.

A QUOTING LAYER BETWEEN YOU AND THE ARTIFACT EDITS THE CONTENT AND REPORTS SUCCESS. Four instances this session: a heredoc'd backslash became a real newline inside a TypeScript string literal (syntax-broken mutant, all twelve tests red, looks exactly like the result you wanted); a heredoc'd regex never compiled so a fixture was never modified and the test passed against it — which read as A FALSE ACCUSATION against a working guard; a backticked word in a hub message was executed as a command substitution and the clause arrived missing its subject; and json.dumps without ensure_ascii=False escaped every em-dash in Aaron's settings.json. WRITE EVERY SCRIPT AND EVERY MESSAGE TO A FILE, including one-liners, and have mutation scripts ASSERT THE EDIT LANDED before running anything.

tsc --noEmit ON EVERY MUTANT, BEFORE COUNTING IT. Three mutants this session were type-invalid and proved nothing while looking red or green as convenient — TS2349 from calling an object instead of its method, and an invented field that fell back to the real one at run time. A mutant that breaks syntax or types is not a mutant.

A FIXTURE CAN FAIL IN THE FLATTERING DIRECTION, and that is harder to see than a vacuous one because it looks like rigour. My first A1 decoy carried all three query terms in one short sentence and beat entry 299; the developer's rank-9 fixture gave every decoy a length advantage. Both exaggerated the defect. Measure your fixture's shape — decoy lengths against the target's — and report the range.

THE DERIVATION READS ELEMENTS, NOT WORDS. `zzqqxxyy 2>&1 | tail -3; echo $?` derives all three terms and injects, because the recogniser sees a trimmer pipeline and a $? read. You cannot produce a SILENT fire with nonsense command text; use a three-document store, where bm25's IDF collapses and nothing clears the floor.

EVERY ROW YOU RUN, RUNS ON THIS MACHINE. CI is the second machine and it found two faults in one file the first time it looked, both of which passed every local run including three full suites. Cite a CI run id as evidence, and treat an empty statusCheckRollup as PRE-REGISTRATION and not a pass — mine was genuinely empty for ~3.5 minutes after the push before the run appeared.

NOTHING IS PUSHED FROM THIS SEAT. The planner pushes QA branches by the SHA this seat reports, on Aaron's word for that push. Every push names a BRANCH TIP, never an interior commit — a report correction is auditable only if the thing it corrects travels with it.

REGISTERING THE HOOK IN ~/.claude/settings.json IS MACHINE-WIDE, not QA-tree-wide: two of the ten fire rows from the A7 probe carry other seats' session uuids. Aaron's word is for THAT ACT AT THAT SHA and does not carry forward.
